neighbours.label: a named mathematical or information-science theory, or the scientist credited with founding it, in expository text ('In graph theory, ...', '... founded by Claude Shannon')
fire: Error-correcting codes owe a great deal to the work of Richard Hamming at Bell Labs.
In number theory, a prime is a whole number with exactly two divisors.
Much of modern statistics rests on ideas introduced by Ronald Fisher.
In set theory, the empty set is a subset of every other set.
The theory of computation was shaped by Alan Turing and Alonzo Church.
In control theory, feedback is used to keep a system stable.
Quantum mechanics was developed by Werner Heisenberg and Erwin Schrodinger.
In chaos theory, tiny changes in the starting conditions can lead to huge differences.
quiet: Error-correcting codes are used every day in phones, satellites and hard drives.
In our village, a market is held every Saturday morning by the church.
Much of modern statistics is taught with computers in the first year.
In the kitchen, the empty jar is kept on the top shelf.
The computer lab was renovated by the university last summer.
In winter, the heating is used to keep the building warm.
Quantum computers are still expensive and difficult to build.
In the story, tiny changes in the plan lead to huge problems for the hero.
